PullRequest.Title: Fix Claude customization migration targets
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Publishes writable Claude `agents`, `skills`, and `rules` directory customizations for every workspace and user scope, including empty directories. This allows the migration service to retain legacy customization candidates that have a valid Claude destination but no existing Claude customization of that type.

Adds focused discovery coverage for empty workspace and user migration targets while preserving coverage of populated directories.

Fixes #334938

## Testing

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/customizations/claudeSessionCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts`

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or refresh a Claude agent session and publish discovered customizations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `getSessionCustomizations` completes existing filesystem scans and, after materialization, the existing SDK snapshot before mapping and publishing the full customization state. The changed mapper only appends three directory descriptors per distinct workspace root plus user scope after those boundaries complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan workspace/user Claude agents, skills, plugins, rules, MCP configuration, and hooks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing scans cover each distinct workspace root plus user scope; cardinality is unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same scans ran before the mapper omitted empty directory descriptors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These scans must complete before the customization snapshot can be mapped and returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the live SDK resolved-customization snapshot after session materialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one snapshot request per customization refresh, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK snapshot request occurred before the changed mapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It is awaited before mapping the result; the changed lines do not add or move this request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish a full-replacement `SessionCustomizationsChanged` state action to consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial publication per session and subsequent publications only when deep equality detects a changed snapshot. Payload gains 3*(R+1) bounded metadata descriptors, not per discovered file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full snapshot was published, omitting absent agent/skill/rule directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication follows discovery; the small added serialization is on the update path but does not introduce an additional boundary call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R distinct workspace roots and discovered customization entries. The diff adds exactly 3*(R+1) small directory objects with empty child arrays when those kinds are absent; typical single-root sessions add at most six descriptors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four discovery scans are already launched with `Promise.all`; multi-root scope scans are also parallel. Per-session publications are sequenced and identical snapshots are coalesced by deep equality. The diff changes neither scheduling nor concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovery is rescanned on the existing session creation/change paths; `_lastCustomizations` retains only the latest snapshot, and unchanged refreshes are suppressed before dispatch. The diff adds no cache, cache key, negative-cache behavior, or unbounded history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code and all callers show only small URI/id/object allocation and bounded full-snapshot serialization; no added filesystem, SDK, subprocess, network, or per-child operation is reachable from the new descriptors.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace-root counts can vary, but the additive payload is three metadata-only records per root and empty children produce no customization rows. No realistic cardinality supports a user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The intended source-folder availability costs O(R) small allocations/bytes and leaves the existing expensive discovery boundaries unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compute migration candidates or choose a destination for agents, skills, and rules
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Migration first performs its existing prompt-file discovery, then calls `provideSourceFolders`; destination picking calls the same provider directly. The newly published empty directories are converted to in-memory folder metadata only, enabling the intended targets.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List existing prompt/customization files used as migration candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing listing calls per migration category/type; unchanged by the new target descriptors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same candidate scans ran, but empty Claude destinations were absent and therefore filtered candidates out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Candidate discovery must complete before migration filtering. The source-folder descriptors trigger no filesystem existence check or directory creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one folder per customization type for each distinct workspace root plus one user folder. Candidate filtering scales with existing candidate count and this bounded root count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Migration types are computed concurrently by the existing `Promise.all`; each migration queries its distinct target types serially, unchanged by this PR. `provideSourceFolders` itself performs a synchronous in-memory loop and starts no concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider reads the current session customization snapshot; no new cache or retained collection is introduced. Empty directories remain in only the current session state snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `provideSourceFolders` only filters descriptors and constructs URI metadata; migration uses them for in-memory compatibility checks, with actual file work outside this changed discovery path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of migration candidates can be large, but the diff changes target availability rather than candidate enumeration or boundary-call count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new descriptors make valid destinations visible without eagerly touching or creating those directories.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render customization management items for a Claude session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The item provider partitions top-level descriptors and iterates directory children. Empty directories contribute zero child items, so no UI row, plugin expansion, or file read is added.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Three empty directory containers per scope when kinds are absent; child cardinality is zero for the newly covered case.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only plugin containers are expanded with `Promise.all`; the new entries are directory containers and never enter that expansion list.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current customization snapshot is read from the service; no additional cache entries or persistent UI nodes are created for empty directory children.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the directory rendering loop traverses `children ?? []`, and these changed descriptors have `children: []`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; there is a small linear metadata classification cost by workspace-root count but no rendering/layout or I/O mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Empty containers are skipped at the child-item layer and do not cause rendering or expansion work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete three-file diff and traced session discovery/publication, migration destination lookup, and customization UI rendering. The PR adds bounded metadata objects and slightly larger state snapshots, but no new expensive boundary, fan-out, eager directory work, concurrency burst, retained growth, or user-visible performance mechanism. No findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
